ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Phillis Wheatley

code.originalText: Asthma review after an exacerbation with a cold on her return from abroad: control, repeat spirometry and FeNO, the winter plan, completion of vaccines, and her changed circumstances

text.paragraph: Asthma review five weeks after an exacerbation with a cold. [S]

Miss Wheatley returns five weeks after the sick visit for asthma with a cold, when she stepped up to budesonide-formoterol as maintenance and reliever. The nurse telephoned her two days later and she was improving; she did not come for the review booked within a week, because she was very busy after her return. She never needed the standby prednisone. Her cold cleared within ten days; she now takes one inhalation twice daily and needs an extra one about once a week, and has not woken at night for three weeks. Her peak flow is 370 to 390 L/min. The screening tests from her preventive visit were negative for HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B surface antigen, and she has no immunity to hepatitis B. She has news she wanted to share: she now holds her own papers and her freedom, and whatever she earns from her book is her own. For now she still lives in the same house. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-26; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; oxygen saturation 99 percent; peak flow 385 L/min
Head, eyes, ears, nose, and throat

Wheeze, cough and breathlessness this winter, for about three months: symptoms on three or four days a week, waking with cough and a tight chest about twice a month, breathless climbing the hill streets in cold air; worse with cold wind, kitchen and fireplace smoke, and colds; called a weak chest and asthma since childhood but never tested or treated. Asthma to be confirmed with spirometry before and after bronchodilator and FeNO
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to her documented frail, asthmatic childhood. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Asthma, confirmed, mild persistent: variable airflow obstruction (FEV1/FVC 0.72, below the lower limit of normal, rising to 0.80 after bronchodilator; FEV1 2.24 L, 83 percent predicted, rising 330 mL or 15 percent); type 2 inflammation (FeNO 38 ppb, blood eosinophils 0.38 x10^3/uL, total IgE 165, house dust mite sensitization); tuberculosis infection test negative and chest X-ray clear. Triggers: cold air, kitchen and fireplace smoke, colds
S — Synthetic modern confirmation linked to her documented frail, asthmatic childhood and her own later descriptions of asthma.

Asthma exacerbation with a cold a week after returning from abroad: three days of wheeze, chest tightness and waking at night despite six to eight reliever inhalations a day; peak flow 270 L/min (68 percent of her best of 400), oxygen saturation 96 percent; 330 L/min after treatment in clinic; treated without oral corticosteroids; resolved
S — Synthetic exacerbation anchored to her own letter describing a cold and asthma after her return; the clinical details are synthetic.
Prone to seasickness on boat trips; meclizine for the sea crossing; resolved on her return
Pregnancy planning: not sexually active and no contraception wanted now; she may wish to have children one day; folic acid by her choice, and asthma care planned before and during any pregnancy
S — Synthetic reproductive health counselling; not a claim about her real life.

list.item:
Asthma, controlled on maintenance and reliever (J45.30). Recovered from the exacerbation without an oral corticosteroid; FEV1 2.45 L (91 percent predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.78 and FeNO 24 ppb are now normal. Her summer away was free of trouble, and colds in cold, damp weather are her main risk, so she stays on maintenance and reliever through the winter and steps back down to as-needed treatment in the spring if she stays well. [S]
Continue budesonide-formoterol one inhalation twice daily and as needed.
Action plan updated for the winter.
Influenza and COVID-19 vaccines for the new season today.
Review in three months; consider stepping down in the spring.

Asthma exacerbation with a cold (J45.31). Resolved. [S]
Problem resolved; the standby prednisone, never used, is stopped and a new course will be written if needed.

Seasickness (T75.3XXA). Meclizine helped in the first days at sea and was finished on her return. [S]
Problem resolved.

Vaccines and screening. Not immune to hepatitis B; other screening negative. [S]
HepB-CpG dose 2 today completes the hepatitis B series.
HPV dose 2 today, delayed by her travel; dose 3 in about three months.

Her changed circumstances. She is now free and responsible for her own living. Her care, her information and her decisions remain hers, as before. [S]
Social work appointment, at her request, for health coverage in her own name, income and housing.
She will tell the clinic if her address or contact details change.
